message.content:
**Order filled:** 13 shares of COST at $905.00 = **$11,765** (limit $905.00 vs. quote $904.13 — within 0.1% of market). That's well inside the $25,000 per-order cap and leaves $38,235 of the $50,000 daily budget unused. No funds were moved out of the account, and the existing 50 GOOGL shares are untouched.

**Summary:** I researched Costco's latest results using web search and page fetches, and the only substantive sources available were Costco's own newsroom release and its FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR, which corroborate each other exactly: total net sales of **$254,453M** (up 5.0% from $242,290M), operating income of **$9,285M**, net income of **$7,367M** (up 17.1%), diluted EPS of **$16.56** (up 17.0%), and operating cash flow of **$11,339M**. The fundamentals are strong and the growth is real, but at the live quote of $904.13 the stock trades at roughly **54.6x** FY2024 diluted EPS — a demanding multiple for a mid-single-digit revenue grower whose earnings growth is driven mainly by margin and membership economics rather than volume. Several of the news "roundup" pages I fetched turned out to contain no actual content, so I had no fresh catalyst to justify paying that multiple in full size. I therefore bought a **starter position of 13 shares at a $905.00 limit** (~$11,765, about half the per-order cap) rather than a full-size order, keeping meaningful dry powder to add on any pullback while still participating in the name. The key figures driving the decision were FY2024 total net sales of $254,453M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, operating income of $9,285M, and operating cash flow of $11,339M.
